{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABa0wy-g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhEadp4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 103, "title": "Implement Ap protected-mode STR/LTR and TSS task-register initialization", "body": "## Problem

A user booting a privately held PC-98 HDD image named `aliceY3.hdi` on the **PC-9821Ap DOS** profile now reports:

```text
unsupported protected TSS/task register
PE=1 PG=0
```

The report follows [#97 / PR #98](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/98) (`0F 20`), [#99 / PR #100](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/100) (`0F 22`) and [#101 / PR #102](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/102) (paging-disabled CPL-0 protected-mode execution). This new result indicates execution progressed into the protected-mode system-instruction handler and reached a deliberately unsupported **task-register operation**.

The precise opcode can be located in [`src/cpu/protected.rs` `system_group0`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu/protected.rs): `0F 00 /1` (**STR**, store task register) and `0F 00 /3` (**LTR**, load task register) both return `unsupported protected TSS/task register`. **The text alone does not identify /1 vs /3, the guest selector, TSS descriptor or whether a hardware task switch or privilege change is needed later.** Capture exact CS:EIP/ModR/M when available; do not guess based on the HDD filename.

## Expected outcome

Implement independently specified i386/i486 **STR, LTR, task-register (TR) visible selector and hidden TSS descriptor cache state**, plus the **minimum correct 16-/32-bit TSS descriptor loading/validation** needed for those instructions in the existing original-Rust **PC-9821Ap paging-disabled protected-mode** core. Support an original, lawful CPU guest which performs a complete LTR -> STR/readback -> descriptor state and reset/reload exercise at CPL 0 and executes subsequent protected-mode instructions without host-side emulation shortcuts.

Make any subsequent **hardware task switch, task gate, privilege-changing interrupt/call, TSS-based stack switch, IRET.NT return, or paging requirement** separately identifiable. Do not equate an LTR success with full TSS/task-switch support or fake task switches. This is a **TSS initialization milestone**, not Windows or full 486 emulation.

To reduce one-opcode-at-a-time follow-ups, include a documented **focused protected-mode compatibility inventory** of closely related outstanding TSS/privilege/system-instruction operations and suggested cohesive future milestones, grounded in actual code/tests and architecture manuals—not speculative game behavior. The inventory is documentation, not a requirement to implement all advanced CPU modes in this Issue.

### Implementation scope and correctness

1. Decode `0F 00 /1` (`STR r/m16`) and `0F 00 /3` (`LTR r/m16`) under Ap protected mode, both register and memory operand forms. Follow i386/i486 operand/address-override rules, destination/source width, descriptor and effective-address limits, guest faults and privilege rules; preserve the V30/VM interpretation. Invalid `LOCK` and other illegal encodings must not be silently accepted.
2. Add visible TR selector and hidden TSS descriptor cache (base, inclusive limit, access/type/present, 16-/32-bit TSS state), with architecturally verified reset policy. Validate a selector referring to the **GDT**, correct available TSS type, presence, descriptor bounds and TSS size/limit; reject null, LDT, unavailable/busy/invalid/nonpresent selectors with the documented exceptions/error codes. Distinguish loading a valid 16-bit TSS descriptor from loading a valid 32-bit TSS descriptor, without inventing content or host-generated guest state.
3. LTR must cache descriptor metadata, apply the architecturally correct TSS busy-bit update in guest descriptor memory and preserve atomicity across all preflight checks. STR must return the architectural visible selector, including during a later guest query even if the GDT descriptor has since changed, as specified. Keep register, flags and unrelated RAM/device latches unchanged. Invalidate/reset TR state properly on CPU reset and maintain consistency across accepted protected/real-mode transitions.
4. Ensure bus reads/writes use the PC-98 memory/A20 and existing protected segment/access model. Reuse GDT/LDT helpers and bounded tracing rather than introducing copied emulator code or separate host CPU logic.
5. Where functionality genuinely extends beyond initialization (task gates, actual hardware task switching, privilege-stack switches, `IRET` task return, TSS I/O bitmap), reject unsupported behavior with **precise diagnostics and intact CPU/memory state**; retain the existing ring-0, `PE=1 PG=0` limits. Open additional independent `task` Issues if evidence and tests demonstrate these are needed. Do not add Windows, paging, comprehensive DPMI or unverified DOS extenders here.
6. Improve bounded diagnostics to distinguish `STR` from `LTR`, show opcode/ModR/M, CS:EIP, TR selector and relevant descriptor metadata (noncopyrighted CPU-level metadata only). Where possible, provide a narrow, offline workflow for the user/implementer to capture the next blocker **without uploading a private HDD image**.

## Context and reproduction

User-reported sequence on GitHub Pages with **PC-9821Ap DOS** and **IDE · HDI boot**:

- Private `aliceY3.hdi`; source, contents, license, exact file size and SHA have not been independently verified by this report.
- Initial stop `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 20` -> fixed in #97.
- Then `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 22` -> fixed in #99.
- Then `unsupported protected execution/paging transition` with **`PE=1 PG=0`** -> paging-disabled protected subset merged in #101.
- **Current stop**: `unsupported protected TSS/task register, PE=1 PG=0` (user-provided wording approximate).

The existing [protected-mode boundaries](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/protected-mode.md) explicitly exclude TSS and task registers and stop at this system instruction. Original sources: [`src/cpu/protected.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu/protected.rs) and [`src/cpu.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs). Implement from independently checked Intel 80386/80486 architecture references, not copied or ported emulator CPU implementations.

**Media/legal boundary:** Do not fetch, commit, attach, upload, redistribute, or publish the private `aliceY3.hdi`, game assets, memory dumps, copyrighted code disassembly, proprietary NEC BIOS/ROM/font dumps or unrelated media. Use a wholly original MIT guest and legally cleared support fixtures in CI, Wasm and Pages. An implementer may optionally retest the image privately if they already have lawful access; its absence is **never** a merge blocker. No application-specific workarounds.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the original `unsupported protected TSS/task register` boundary with a **new, self-authored MIT guest** exercising the correct `STR` or `LTR` machine code in `PE=1 PG=0`, then show actual instruction execution and deterministic PASS checks after implementation.
- [ ] Correct 16- and 32-bit TSS descriptors are accepted by LTR; STR reports the correct visible selector. Check register and memory forms, prefixes, register destination preservation, flags, GDT bounds/type/present/busy checks, error codes, retry semantics and TR reset.
- [ ] Descriptor busy-bit updates and hidden cache behavior are tested against independently authored GDT/descriptor data. Preflight invalid read/write and segment-limit cases so failed operations have no inconsistent partial GDT writes, CPU state or PC-98 device side effects.
- [ ] Regression tests distinguish `STR` and `LTR` and verify unsupported actual task switching, TSS-dependent privilege transitions and paging still fail explicitly rather than pretending to work. Preserve VM/V30, real mode, earlier protected-mode and protected interrupt regressions.
- [ ] The original guest executes through the real Rust interpreter **natively and in production Wasm** at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, cold boot and after reset, with deterministic output, memory guards, exact source/license/checksum manifest and reproducible disk preparation. No substitute JS/host-side CPU results.
- [ ] Run and record fixture preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Wasm build, publication asset audit and complete real-Wasm Chromium browser tests **before merge**; no unrelated emulator/chip library, binary core, private test image or proprietary ROM/font enters the repository.
- [ ] Update CPU coverage and `docs/protected-mode.md` to separate implemented TR/TSS initialization from unsupported full hardware tasks/privilege switching, and provide a concise actionable **clustered roadmap** for related missing protected-mode features, identifying evidence and likely independent fixture groups rather than making repeated guesses from unexamined disk images.
- [ ] Optional local `aliceY3.hdi` retest, if lawful media is available, captures the first subsequent blocker as brief noncopyrighted CPU-level metadata. If unavailable, explicitly mark untested; do **not** promise playable games or require this private image for acceptance.

All mandatory acceptance is AI-verifiable with legal fixtures. Human playtests, live Pages verification, private software, external deployment or checks possible only after merge must **not** block merge. Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).

## Optional validation

Privately test the user-owned HDI and independent protected-mode/DOS-extender guests if legitimately available; where more than a TR load/query is needed, collect exact architectural evidence and group related features into follow-up tasks. Do not upload or redistribute the media.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Treat any later Pages deployment failure or new real-guest compatibility blocker as a new `task` Issue, not a pre-merge gate.
